name: The Field household at 1905 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_field_marshall

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1905 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1905 Marshall Field.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1905, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The five live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. A coachman's wife and children in the rear building are named in his note rather than carded. The children the Blue Book lists at the number from 1890 to 1911 are on the card with the years each was listed, whether or not they were at home in 1904. The 1910 census was not read for this card. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Marshall Field
persons.note: The 1900 census lists Marshall Field here as head, born August 1834, in Massachusetts, widowed, dry goods merchant (ED 40, sheet 4A, line 34, leaf n800).

persons.name: Marshall Field jr.
persons.note: Marshall Field's only surviving son (a brother, Louis, died as a baby in 1866). He was at home here at seventeen, for the children's party his parents gave on 1 January 1886. He married Albertine Huck and by the 1892 edition of the Blue Book the couple had their own house a few doors south at 1919, where they live in 1904 on their own card. He died in 1905.

persons.name: Ethel Field

born.note: Born in Cook County, Illinois, in 1873 (Wikipedia).

persons.note: Marshall Field's daughter, twelve at the children's party of 1 January 1886 in this house. She was married here, at 'the home of her parents, 1905 Prairie Avenue', to Arthur Magie Tree on 1 January 1891, and was later Countess Beatty.

born.note: The census gives September 1858, age 42 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Cook" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (cook); born September 1858 (the figures are hard to read), in Sweden, came to the United States in 1889, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.
